(Studio: Katie Couric)  A new report from the International Monetary Fund on the world economy, a cut in the federal interest rate and another drop in the stock market noted.  

(Studio: Anthony Mason)  The sixth day of the tumbling of the market featured; details given about the coordinated cut in interest rates by the US, Canada, England, Sweden and Switzerland, the drop in overseas markets and wrecked retail sales figures.  [MAN&nbsp- says there is no confidence out there.]  [PNC Financial Services Group economist Stuart HOFFMAN†- says the Fed is throwing stuff on the wall.]  [Treasury Secretary Henry PAULSON&nbsp- says challenges remain ahead.]  [At a Los Angeles store, CUSTOMER, OWNER&nbsp- comment.]  

(Studio: Katie Couric)  A burst of activity in the housing market noted; statistics on Americans owing more than their houses are worth cited.  

(Chicago: Cynthia Bowers)  The plight of homeowners examined; details given about the settlement by Countrywide that may lead to a readjustment of payments and of coping tips for the mortgage crisis.  [Music teacher homeowner Keith McEACHRON†- says every dollar goes to his mortgage.]  [Illinois attorney general Lisa MADIGAN†- says we have a modern program.]  [MAN&nbsp- offers advice.]  

(Studio: Katie Couric)  An additional loan from the Fed to the struggling AIG insurance company noted.

(Studio: Katie Couric)  The return of presidential candidates Senators Barack Obama and John McCain to the campaign trail after last night's debate introduced.  

(Chicago: Dean Reynolds)  Obama's message of optimism in the economic crisis featured; scenes shown of Obama shaking hands with the people; details given about his money advantage.  [In Indianapolis, OBAMA  - says we can steer ourselves out of this crisis.]  

(Studio: Katie Couric)  Report introduced.  

(Strongsville, Ohio: Chip Reid)  The attack campaign by McCain and Governor Sarah Palin against Obama featured; scenes shown from a Palin rally in Ohio.  [McCAIN - asks why Obama voted to raise taxes.]  The criticism of Obama from wife Cindy McCain noted.  

(Studio: Katie Couric)  A Reality Check report introduced.  

(Washington: Wyatt Andrews)  A fact check of what McCain and Obama said in last night's debate presented; details given about McCain's mortgage purchase plan and about Obama's claim on spending while cutting the budget.  [McCAIN - speaks about buying up mortgages; admits it is expensive.]  [September 23, OBAMA - suggests allowing the government to purchase mortgages directly.]  How neither candidate has admitted to a change in plans despite the government's new trillion dollar spending noted.

(Studio: Katie Couric)  The series, "Presidential Questions," to give you a better sense of who Senators John McCain and Barack Obama are re-introduced.  

(Studio: Katie Couric)  The two presidential candidates' views on the best and the worst thing that has ever happened to this country and who are the three people you would like to have dinner with,  [McCAIN - says our founding was the best thing that ever happened with the creation of a model document with the worst thing being the Great Depression.]  [OBAMA - says the starting premise of America was the best thing that happened that became the North star for us and the world with the worst being slavery and the treatment of native Americans.]  [OBAMA - says he would love to have dinner with former South African President Nelson Mandela, who is getting frail, Warren Buffett, who is a good economic adviser and really smart and with his grandmother, who has been the rock of his family and cannot now travel.]  [McCAIN - says Gen. David Petraeus has been inspiring and fascinating, Meg Whitman, who built eBay and understands the American dream and any major league sports figure like Michael Phelps or American wrestler Henry Cejudo%.]  

(Studio: Katie Couric)  Tomorrow's Where They Stand segment previewed.
